children.title: Cash flow hedges

children.summary: This section details the accounting policy for cash flow hedges, specifically focusing on interest rate swaps used to hedge against interest rate risk associated with forecasted payments and obligations. It explains that changes in fair value are recognized in accumulated other comprehensive income and reclassified into earnings when the hedged transaction affects earnings. The text also notes the election of optional expedients under ASC 848 'Reference Rate Reform' regarding existing interest rate swaps.

children.title: Net investment hedges
children.path: Alibaba Fiscal Year 2026 Interim Report.pdf/Root/DEFINITIONS/2. Summary of significant accounting policies (Continued)/(d) Derivatives and hedging/Net investment hedges
children.summary: This section details the company's accounting policies for net investment hedges. It explains that cross currency swap (CCS) contracts and RMB-denominated senior notes are used to hedge foreign currency risk associated with investments in PRC subsidiaries. The text describes how changes in fair value due to spot exchange rate fluctuations are recognized in accumulated other comprehensive income, while excluding certain components from effectiveness assessments. It also notes a loss of RMB1,279 million recognized in accumulated other comprehensive income for the six months ended September 30, 2025.

children.title: (e) Borrowings
children.path: Alibaba Fiscal Year 2026 Interim Report.pdf/Root/DEFINITIONS/2. Summary of significant accounting policies (Continued)/(e) Borrowings
children.summary: The section details the accounting policies for borrowings, which include bank borrowings, unsecured senior notes, convertible unsecured senior notes, and exchangeable bonds. It explains that these are recognized initially at fair value net of fees and costs, with related accretion recorded as interest expense using the effective interest method. Additionally, it specifies that convertible unsecured senior notes are accounted for entirely as liabilities without separate accounting for the conversion feature under ASC 815, while exchangeable bonds are accounted for under the fair value option.

It describes four specific Accounting Standards Updates (ASUs): ASU 2025-05 regarding credit losses for accounts receivable, ASU 2025-06 concerning internal-use software, ASU 2025-08 on purchased loans, and ASU 2025-09 covering hedge accounting improvements. For each update, the text outlines the scope of the amendments, effective dates ranging from 2027 to 2029, and notes that the company is evaluating the impact of adoption.

The section also states gross goodwill balances and accumulated impairment losses as of March 31 and September 30, 2025.

children.title: 12. Supplier Finance Programs
children.path: Alibaba Fiscal Year 2026 Interim Report.pdf/Root/DEFINITIONS/12. Supplier Finance Programs
children.summary: This section details the Company's supplier finance programs, where suppliers can sell payment obligations to financial institutions for early funding. It notes that the Company generally does not provide assets as security or guarantees under these programs, except for a pledge of treasury investments valued at RMB1,500 million as of March 31, 2025. A table presents the outstanding payment obligations recorded within accrued expenses and bank borrowings as of March 31 and September 30, 2025.

children.title: 13. Convertible unsecured senior notes
children.path: Alibaba Fiscal Year 2026 Interim Report.pdf/Root/DEFINITIONS/13. Convertible unsecured senior notes
children.summary: This page contains Note 13 from the Notes to Unaudited Condensed Consolidated Financial Statements for Alibaba Group Holding Limited, covering the six months ended September 30, 2024 and 2025. The text details the terms of two convertible unsecured senior note issuances: the '2024 Convertible Senior Notes' issued in May 2024 and the '2025 Convertible Senior Notes' issued in September 2025. It outlines principal amounts, maturity dates, interest rates, conversion rates into ADSs, redemption rights, repurchase options, and financial metrics such as unamortized debt discounts and effective interest rates.

children.path: Alibaba Fiscal Year 2026 Interim Report.pdf/Root/DEFINITIONS/13. Convertible unsecured senior notes (Continued)
children.summary: This section details the capped call transactions entered into by Alibaba Group Holding Limited in connection with the issuance of its 2024 and 2025 Convertible Senior Notes. It specifies the costs incurred (US$638 million for 2024 notes and US$184 million for 2025 notes) to reduce potential dilution or offset cash payments upon conversion. The text also outlines the initial cap prices per ADS ($161.60 for 2024 notes and $235.46 for 2025 notes) and notes that these transactions may be settled in cash at the Company's election.

children.title: 14. Exchangeable bonds
children.path: Alibaba Fiscal Year 2026 Interim Report.pdf/Root/DEFINITIONS/14. Exchangeable bonds
children.summary: This section details the issuance of HKD-denominated zero coupon exchangeable bonds by Alibaba Group Holding Limited in July 2025, referencing ordinary shares of its subsidiary, Alibaba Health Information Technology Limited. It outlines key terms including the aggregate principal amount (HK$12 billion), maturity date (July 9, 2032), and initial exchange rate (approximately 160,513.6 AH Shares per HK$1,000,000). The text further describes conditions for adjusting the exchange rate, redemption rights for both the Company and bondholders, a stock borrowing arrangement with bookrunner affiliates to facilitate hedging, and financial impacts such as losses recorded for the six months ended September 30, 2025.

children.summary: This page contains Notes 15 and 16 from the unaudited condensed consolidated financial statements of Alibaba Group Holding Limited for the six months ended September 30, 2024 and 2025. Note 15 details amendments to bank borrowings, including changes to syndicated loan facilities and revolving credit agreements. Note 16 outlines related party transactions with Ant Group and its affiliates, presenting a table that compares amounts earned by and incurred by the Company in RMB millions for the periods ending September 30, 2024 and 2025.

children.title: 17. Risks and contingencies
children.path: Alibaba Fiscal Year 2026 Interim Report.pdf/Root/DEFINITIONS/17. Risks and contingencies
children.summary: This page contains Section 17, 'Risks and contingencies,' from the Notes to Unaudited Condensed Consolidated Financial Statements for Alibaba Group Holding Limited for the six months ended September 30, 2024 and 2025. The text details four primary risk factors: (a) legal restrictions on foreign ownership in China's value-added telecommunications sector and the company's reliance on Variable Interest Entities (VIEs); (b) macro-economic and regulatory uncertainties within the PRC market; (c) potential negative impacts arising from the company's association with Ant Group; and (d) currency risks related to RMB transactions and foreign exchange controls.

children.path: Alibaba Fiscal Year 2026 Interim Report.pdf/Root/DEFINITIONS/17. Risks and contingencies (Continued)

The text details various risks including strategic investments, credit risk concentration in financial instruments, a trade assurance program on international marketplaces, legal proceedings involving AliExpress and the EU Commission, the impact of the Russia-Ukraine conflict on supply chains, and potential sanctions related to export controls and technology restrictions.

children.title: (i) Consolidation and business combinations
children.path: Alibaba Fiscal Year 2026 Interim Report.pdf/Root/DEFINITIONS/22. Reconciliations between U.S. GAAP and International Financial Reporting Standards (Continued)/(i) Consolidation and business combinations
children.summary: This page contains the 'Notes to Unaudited Condensed Consolidated Financial Statements' for Alibaba Group Holding Limited for the six months ended September 30, 2024 and 2025. It features a detailed reconciliation table comparing U.S. GAAP financial figures to International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) for the period ending September 30, 2025, covering items such as revenue, operating income, and net income in millions of RMB. The lower section provides explanatory text regarding accounting policies for consolidation, business combinations, noncontrolling interests, and goodwill impairment.

children.title: (ii) Equity securities without readily determinable fair value
children.path: Alibaba Fiscal Year 2026 Interim Report.pdf/Root/DEFINITIONS/22. Reconciliations between U.S. GAAP and International Financial Reporting Standards (Continued)/(ii) Equity securities without readily determinable fair value
children.summary: The section explains the accounting treatment for equity securities without readily determinable fair values under U.S. GAAP and IFRS. Under U.S. GAAP, the Company can elect to measure these investments at cost less impairment, with adjustments for observable price changes recognized in income statements. Under IFRS, these investments are measured at fair value with changes recognized in income statements.

children.title: (iii) Equity method investments
children.path: Alibaba Fiscal Year 2026 Interim Report.pdf/Root/DEFINITIONS/22. Reconciliations between U.S. GAAP and International Financial Reporting Standards (Continued)/(iii) Equity method investments
children.summary: This section outlines the accounting treatment for equity method investments, explaining that the Company applies the equity method to investments where it has significant influence. It details the criteria for presuming significant influence under U.S. GAAP (limited partnerships or unincorporated entities) versus IFRS (over 20% of voting rights). Additionally, it describes how the Company records its share of post-acquisition results and adjusts for basis differences between carrying values and proportionate shares of net assets.

children.title: (iv) Share-based awards
children.path: Alibaba Fiscal Year 2026 Interim Report.pdf/Root/DEFINITIONS/22. Reconciliations between U.S. GAAP and International Financial Reporting Standards (Continued)/(iv) Share-based awards
children.summary: The section details the accounting treatment for share-based awards held by employees of Alibaba Group Holding Limited, which relate to an equity method investee. It contrasts U.S. GAAP and IFRS: under U.S. GAAP, costs are recognized over the service period with fair value changes in income statements, while under IFRS, they are not considered share-based payments and costs are unrecognized. Additionally, it explains that deferred taxes for these awards are measured based on compensation expenses under U.S. GAAP but on estimated future tax deductions under IFRS.

children.title: (v) Operating leases
children.path: Alibaba Fiscal Year 2026 Interim Report.pdf/Root/DEFINITIONS/22. Reconciliations between U.S. GAAP and International Financial Reporting Standards (Continued)/(v) Operating leases
children.summary: The section titled 'Operating leases' explains the accounting treatment differences between U.S. GAAP and IFRS regarding lease expenses. Under U.S. GAAP, amortization of right-of-use assets and interest expense are combined into a single straight-line lease expense. In contrast, under IFRS, these components are recognized separately: right-of-use assets are amortized on a straight-line basis, while interest expense is recognized using the effective interest method.

children.title: (vi) Redeemable noncontrolling interests
children.path: Alibaba Fiscal Year 2026 Interim Report.pdf/Root/DEFINITIONS/22. Reconciliations between U.S. GAAP and International Financial Reporting Standards (Continued)/(vi) Redeemable noncontrolling interests
children.summary: This section explains the accounting treatment of redeemable equity interests issued by certain subsidiaries. Under U.S. GAAP, these interests are classified as mezzanine equity if redemption is outside the Company's control, or as noncontrolling interests if mandatorily redeemable only upon liquidation. Under IFRS, such redeemable equity interests are generally classified as financial liabilities.

children.title: (vii) Hyperinflation
children.path: Alibaba Fiscal Year 2026 Interim Report.pdf/Root/DEFINITIONS/22. Reconciliations between U.S. GAAP and International Financial Reporting Standards (Continued)/(vii) Hyperinflation
children.summary: This section outlines the accounting treatment for subsidiaries operating in highly inflationary economies under U.S. GAAP and IFRS. Under U.S. GAAP, financial statements are remeasured prospectively as if the functional currency were that of the immediate parent company. Under IFRS, they are restated in terms of the measuring unit current at the end of the reporting period.

children.title: (viii) Convertible unsecured senior notes and instruments in an entity’s own equity
children.path: Alibaba Fiscal Year 2026 Interim Report.pdf/Root/DEFINITIONS/22. Reconciliations between U.S. GAAP and International Financial Reporting Standards (Continued)/(viii) Convertible unsecured senior notes and instruments in an entity’s own equity
children.summary: This section details the accounting treatment differences between U.S. GAAP and IFRS regarding convertible unsecured senior notes and instruments in an entity's own equity. Under U.S. GAAP, convertible notes are treated entirely as liabilities measured at amortized cost, while under IFRS, they may be classified as hybrid financial liabilities if the company can settle in cash. The text also explains that for an instrument to be classified as equity, it must meet a 'fixed-for-fixed' test; however, settlement alternatives permitted under U.S. GAAP often result in asset or liability classification under IFRS.
